title: Homily LXIX
subtitle: Matthew LXIX. 20:29
author: chrysostom
excerpt: Homily LXXII. Matt. XXIII. 1-3. “Then spake Jesus to the multitudes and to His disciples, saying, The Scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: all therefore whatsoever they bid you do, that do;[The Greek text in this clause differs somewhat both from the received and from that followed in the R.V.—R.]but do not after their works.” Then. When? When He had said these things, when He had stopped their mouths; when He had brought them that they should no more dare to tempt Him; when He had shown their state incurable. And since He had made mention of “the Lord” and “my Lord,”[κυρου κα κυρου, referring to the two uses of the word in the Old Testament passage cited in Matt. xxii. 44, but not in precise terms.—R.] He recurs again to the law. And yet the law said nothing of this kind, but, “The Lord thy God is one Lord.”Deut. vi. 4. But Scripture calls the whole Old Testament the law. But these things He saith, showing by all things His full agreement with Him that begat Him. For if He were opposed, He would have said the opposite about the law; but now He commands so great...
